findings.F1: The book fails on its falls, not on its gain or its fees. Its chained maximum drawdown is -82.5% against about 0.62 a year of mean daily return (0.0017/day, sd 0.041, 2,898 book days). It is long-only and moves almost one-for-one with the market: mean +0.0234 on days the coins' average rose (1,551 days) and -0.0233 on days it fell (1,347 days).
findings.F2: On the book's worst 5% of days it lost -10.0% while the coins' average lost -7.3%. On those days 89% of coins were held, against 59% on an average day, and only 36% of coins were in a 50-day uptrend. The big falls come from being fully long into a market-wide drop.
findings.F3: The losing periods are the bear phases. 2018 summed -1.41 and 2022 -0.55 in book daily returns, against coin-average sums of -1.26 and -0.67. Window w14 summed -1.01 with a -73% drawdown inside it, and w7 and w9 summed -0.51 and -0.56.
findings.F4: Gains come from coins in a 50-day uptrend. When a coin was 50-day uptrending, its held days earned 0.00419 a day (t 3.86, n 4,258 coin-days). When it was 50-day downtrending, held days earned 0.00144 (t 0.82, n 1,935). Yet the book was still exposed 38% of the time in downtrends.
findings.F5: The breakout's drift is concentrated in uptrends. Over non-overlapping 10-bar periods, new 20-day highs beat the coin's all-window mean by 0.0367 when the coin's 50-day return was positive (t 2.65, n 200), against 0.0192 when it was negative (t 1.22, n 98). The overall figure is 0.0212 (t 2.45, n 446).
findings.F6: Fees are not the cause; whipsaw is. There were 3,269 long trades with a median hold of 16 days, and their mean gross was +4.37% against 0.29% commission. The 1,563 trades held 15 days or less all lost: net sums of -403, -1,072, -2,027 and -2,872 across the shorter hold buckets. The 1,705 trades held longer than 15 days carried +20,336.
findings.F7: A larger forecast earns more. Next-bar returns were 0.00266 when the forecast was 15-20 (5,047 bars) and 0.00209 when it was 10-15 (2,155 bars). They were -0.00026 at 0-5 (1,319 bars) and 0.00003 at 5-10 (1,734 bars).
findings.F8: Calm downtrends are the one losing state in the book's contribution. Coin-days in a 50-day downtrend with the lowest-tercile 20-day volatility contributed -0.376, while uptrend coin-days contributed +1.18, +1.07 and +0.71 across the three volatility terciles.

ideas.idea: A new 20-day closing high in a coin whose close is above its close of 50 days earlier is followed by a 10-day return above the coin's average. The drift belongs to breakouts inside an established uptrend.
ideas.consequence: Take breakout longs only when the coin's 50-day trend is up, and refuse them in 50-day downtrends, where most of the bear-phase drawdown was taken.
ideas.name: breakout drift needs uptrend

ideas.idea: A coin whose close stays in the top of its 20-day range keeps rising on the following days. The excess return lives in closes pinned at the high, not in closes that drift back into the middle of the range.
ideas.consequence: Hold only while the close sits at the very top of its range, and let the weak, mid-range readings go flat rather than entering and exiting on them.
ideas.name: pinned-at-high closes keep rising

ideas.idea: A new 20-day closing high reached in a calm coin (low 20-day volatility) that is in a 50-day downtrend is followed by a fall back below the high over the next days.
ideas.consequence: Refuse breakout longs in calm downtrending coins, the one state where the book's contribution was negative.
ideas.name: calm downtrend breakouts fade
